title.narrative: Support to WFP Logistics Cluster with the deployment of helicopters and along with other essential common services (transport by fixed-wing aircraft)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian crisis in Somalia is worsening due to devastating floods caused by the El Nino weather phenomenon along the Juba and Shabelle rivers. This has led to severe logistical challenges, damaging transport infrastructure and hindering humanitarian access in Jubaland, South-West State, and Hirshabelle. Currently, 15 out of 19 airstrips in these states are inaccessible, and critical bridges in various locations have been washed away or damaged.ltbrgtSecurity challenges persist due to the presence of non-state armed groups, impeding safe passage and humanitarian operations. Cholera outbreaks are imminent, requiring urgent transportation of medical supplies to Jubbaland, South-West State, and Hir-Shabelle.ltbrgtResponse StrategyltbrgtIn this context, considering the rapidly increasing needs, the Logistics Cluster urgently requires continued deployment two helicopters at least until February 2024, along with other essential common services (transport by fixed wing aircraft) for sustained transport of lifesaving supplies. Specifically, the Logistics Cluster has the following critical requirement for the next two months:ltbrgt1) Sustained helicopter operation: Continued deployment of two helicopters until February 2024, along with essential common services like fixed-wing aircraft for transporting lifesaving supplies. The critical requirements for the next two months include sustained helicopter operations for cargo transport, boat transport, and passenger flights. The helicopter is currently supporting 12 partners in transporting critical cargo to flood-affected areas. Boat transport involves moving boats from Aden Adde International Airport to locations along the Juba and Hirshabelle rivers. Additionally, the helicopter is used for missions to assess flood damage and transport passengers for technical operations.ltbrgt2) Sustained fixed-wing operation and other common services: The Logistics Cluster has a backlog of 1,000 metric tons of cargo, including 686 metric tons of food and non-food items awaiting transport. This backlog is attributed to a single helicopter and an illegal levy imposed in September hindering supply movement. The fixed-wing transport capacity of the two helicopters is insufficient to clear the backlog or meet anticipated needs. The Logistics Cluster requires resources for additional transport options (fixed-wing, road, and sea) to clear the backlog and support partners responding to the floods.ltbrgt3) Humanitarian Logistics Hub Baidoa: A humanitarian logistics hub is being established in Baidoa to enhance capacity and facilitate efficient cargo distribution to flood-affected areas. This includes a WFP Mobile Storage Unit, with operational costs amounting to $160,000 for two months. The hub is expected to significantly improve response efficiency by allowing two to three rotations per day from Baidoa to flood-affected areas in Jubbaland stateltbrgtlt/pgt
